summary: The Ankada Dhodh at Vangan village near Vansda — a vlog-discovered border fall, with the Gandavle hill viewpoint above the same village.
description:
Vangan's Ankada Dhodh had a small vlog moment — 'newly discovered beautiful location, sixteen kilometres from Vansda' — and the map has since caught up with pins for the falls, its twin Advait a short walk east, and the Gandavle hill above the village for those who want a viewpoint with their waterfall. Administratively this is Vansda taluka of Navsari; experientially it belongs to the same western forest orbit as Vansda National Park and Janki Van.

Expect a village-lane approach, a forest walk in, and monsoon-only flow. The Gandavle climb is the add-on for clear days — village fields and border forest from above.
highlights: Advait falls and the Gandavle hill viewpoint in the same village
Rounds out the Vansda–Waghai western day

modes.road: Village lanes ~16 km from Vansda town; the falls, Advait and the Gandavle hill share the approach
modes.rail: Waghai/Bilimora heritage-line side; Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Forest walk from the village lane; the hill is a separate short climb

visit.notes: Falls in the morning, Gandavle hill if the sky is clear.

seasonality.notes: Monsoon-fed; the hill viewpoint stays worthwhile into winter.

experience.photography_notes: The falls take tight forest frames; Gandavle gives the wide one.

amenities.food: Vansda town, sixteen kilometres, has the nearest food
amenities.guides: Village youths point or walk along

warnings: Wet rock is slick — grip footwear
The Gandavle slopes are open — avoid in lightning weather

tips: Do falls, Advait and the hill as one village outing
Combine with Janki Van or Vansda NP for the full western day
